post-1.title: Warm chamomile tea + hot water bottle saved my Day 1 cramps today
post-1.content: Just wanted to share a gentle reminder to anyone having a tough Day 1. Chamomile tea with a pinch of ginger and resting flat on my back with a hot water bag reduced my pain level from an 8 to a 3. Please take it easy today!

post-2.title: First time using a menstrual cup — here is what helped me seal it correctly!
post-2.content: I was so nervous for months! What finally worked for me was the punch-down fold instead of C-fold, and relaxing my shoulders completely. If you are struggling on your first try, don’t panic! Take a deep breath and try in the shower.

post-3.title: Day 24 luteal phase anxiety — does anyone else feel super sensitive right now?
post-3.content: Every small thing feels a bit heavier today. I know it’s just progesterone dropping, but knowing doesn’t always stop the feeling. Holding space for anyone else feeling emotional in their pre-period phase.

comments.c-1: Chamomile tea is so soothing! Adding a tiny drop of honey makes it even better.
comments.c-2: Sending virtual warmth! Rest up today 💕
comments.c-3: Punch-down fold is definitely the game-changer! So proud of you for trying!
comments.c-4: You are so not alone. Luteal phase sensitivity is so real. Be extra gentle with yourself today 💕

insights.daysOverdueText: {{days}} day(s) later than your recent estimate
insights.onTrack: Your cycle timing is currently within your expected estimate.
insights.lateNoticeGeneric: Your period is currently later than your recent estimate. Cycle timing can naturally vary due to routine, stress, or lifestyle context.
insights.lateNoticeIllnessMed: Your period is later than your recent estimate. You also logged an illness or medication earlier this cycle. Changes in health, stress, sleep and routine can sometimes coincide with cycle changes, although we can't determine from your logs whether they caused the delay.
insights.lateNoticeStressLifestyle: Your period is later than your recent estimate. You logged higher stress or routine changes earlier this cycle. These are helpful pieces of personal context to keep in your health history.
insights.disclaimerNoCausation: These are useful pieces of context, but they don't tell us exactly why your period is later. Cycle timing can naturally vary.
insights.doctorSuggestion: If your period is delayed by over a week or you experience severe discomfort, consider consulting a healthcare professional for general peace of mind.
insights.patternsTitle: Things You Logged Around Your Cycles
insights.patternsSub: Over recent cycles, Sakhi has compiled these observational context entries:
insights.observationalNote: These observations reflect your logged context over time and are for your personal reference, not a medical diagnosis.

pattern.level1Title: Your cycle looks consistent with your recent pattern
pattern.level1Message: Keep tracking — your cycle history helps Sakhi give you more personalized estimates over time.
pattern.level2Title: Your cycle looks a little different this time
pattern.level2Message: One cycle that is earlier or later than your recent pattern can happen for many reasons, such as routine shifts, sleep changes, or stress. Keep tracking so Sakhi can understand your usual pattern better.
pattern.level3Title: We've noticed that your cycle has been irregular more than once
pattern.level3Message: Cycle timing can vary for many reasons, including stress, changes in sleep or routine, illness, weight shifts, exercise, contraception, and other health factors. Since this pattern has happened repeatedly, it may be helpful to discuss your cycle history with a gynecologist or other qualified healthcare professional.
pattern.stableConfirmation: Logged history is active & updating automatically
pattern.historySub: Summary of established baseline and logged cycle variations
pattern.historyDisclaimer: Tracking your cycle history helps Sakhi observe your usual range. Occasional variation is common, while repeated pattern changes are good to share with your gynaecologist.
